newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore HSFO to rise with futures, tight Mideast.
newsitem.headline: Singapore HSFO to rise with futures, tight Mideast.

text.p: High sulphur fuel oil prices were expected to edge up with the strong gains seen on the product and crude futures markets and limited MidEast supplies, traders said on Friday.

Singapore September fuel oil paper firmed with the overnight hike in crude to $107.25/$108.50 from $106.00/$107.00. Traders said they expected talking levels for wet cargoes to range from $105-$106 per tonne.
Traders said a prompt Kuwaiti cargo of 380 cst was sold this week at a $2.00-discount to MidEast spot 180 cst quotes.
"It is very pricey," said a trader. "But it is possible, seeing 380 cst supplies in Singapore are tight." The price differential between the 180 and 380 cst has narrowed to $4 a tonne.
Traders said there were cargoes available in the MidEast, mainly Iranian, but sellers are now asking for higher prices.

Sellers of MidEast cargoes were also being encouraged to demand higher levels as India emerged with its fourth 25,000-tonne cargo of 180 cst for September this week. The tender which closes September 5 requires the cargo to be delivered September 25-29 to Goa/Kandla on the Indian west coast.
Traders said the requirement would be covered from Fujairah in the Mideast rather than from Singapore.
Some traders said India is possibly seeking the fuel oil as a result of the shutdown of the 160,000 barrels-per-day Mathura refinery from September 3-30.

Good demand for bunkers in Fujairah has also supported the 380 cst market. Shipowners have been deterred by high Singapore bunker prices and have sought supplies at other bunker centres, traders said.
Chinese demand was heard to be picking up for second-half September deliveries into southern China. But traders said "pricing problems", or low bids of $108-$110 per tonne has stopped any trade.
